acceptance.contender_b_post_advance_rule: After contender A advances, fetch CURRENT again. If observed version is not 60 or observed blob is not the initial v60 blob, reject contender B before any claim, event, or CURRENT write.
acceptance.duplicate_rule: An existing deterministic claim path is DUPLICATE; do not replace the claim and do not advance CURRENT.
acceptance.pointer_gate: Exact claim readback; immutable event create and exact readback; second CURRENT fetch must remain exact v60/blob 80fcd1fa57d1d44458424d43c2e10db393c141e0/projection digest 6a445b5c921a2433e417d3ab4cc83f100f4c15030ba9e0d4316cbac0394dac3c; then one blob-SHA-guarded CURRENT replacement; final readback must be v61.

canonical_transition.honest_flaw: This is a sequential two-contender simulation, not simultaneous execution. It demonstrates fail-closed revalidation after one observed advance but does not prove fairness or safety under arbitrary network delay, force-push, rebase, alternate branches, compromised writers, or API anomalies. Claim, event, CURRENT, conflict receipt, reads, and Slack are separate effects. Git supplies no cross-file transaction, database isolation, linearizability, exactly-once execution, or automatic orphan repair.

probe.name: TWO_CONTENDERS_SHARED_V60_POST_ADVANCE_REVALIDATION_V1
probe.result: Two contenders are modeled from the same exact v60 observation. Contender A is bound to the accepted transition. Contender B has no write authority after A advances and must be rejected by a fresh exact-version check; a separate immutable conflict receipt will record the post-advance observation.

canonical_transition.rollback: Never delete the immutable claim, accepted event, or conflict receipt. If the accepted transition is later found invalid, append a compensating transition from the then-current exact version and replace CURRENT only with its exact then-current blob SHA.
